newsitem.title: UK: Freepages says non-exec chair Zimet resigns.
newsitem.headline: Freepages says non-exec chair Zimet resigns.

text.p: Ronald Zimet has resigned as non-executive chairman of Freepages Group Plc and will be replaced with immediate effect by Dick Eykel, the British information services group said on Monday.
"The board of Freepages has today been informed by Mr Ronald Zimet of his decision to resign as non-executive chairman and from the board of Freepages, with immediate effect," Freepages said.

Zimet's name has been widely reported in the British press in recent weeks because he was named in correspondence over a 2.4 million stg controversial payment during 31-year-old entrepreneur Andrew Regan's failed 1.2 billion stg bid for Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society.

Freepages gave no reason for Zimet's decision to resign his position but said that trading in the current year had "so far been slightly ahead of directors' expecations" and sales in both classified and corporate products continued "to develop favourably resulting in rapid revenue growth".

The group also said it was currently negotiating with a number of international parties to form complementary strategic alliances. "Further announcements will be made at such time as may be appropriate," it added.
